title: Why chicken and broccoli Works So Well Together
flavorProfile: Chicken delivers mild, savory umami depth while broccoli contributes earthy bitterness and natural sweetness. When paired with garlic, ginger, or soy sauce, the combination achieves a balanced profile: salty-umami from the poultry, subtle sweetness from the cruciferous florets, and a fresh, slightly peppery finish that prevents palate fatigue.
nutritionalSynergy: Chicken provides complete protein, B12, niacin, and selenium, while broccoli supplies vitamin C, K, folate, and sulforaphane. Vitamin C in broccoli enhances non-heme iron absorption from chicken, increasing bioavailability by up to 67%. The combination also supports collagen synthesis (vitamin C + amino acids) and offers synergistic antioxidant effects—broccoli's glucosinolates complement chicken's cysteine for detoxification support.
prepTechniques: Cut chicken into uniform bite-sized pieces and marinate in soy sauce, rice vinegar, and cornstarch for 15 minutes to tenderize and lock in moisture.
Blanch broccoli florets in salted boiling water for 90 seconds, then shock in ice water to preserve bright color and crisp-tender texture.
Stir-fry chicken over high heat until golden, add garlic and ginger, then toss in broccoli with a sauce of oyster sauce, sesame oil, and a pinch of sugar for glaze.

faq.a: Refrigerate in an airtight container within 2 hours; consume within 3–4 days. Freeze for up to 3 months, but note broccoli may soften upon thawing—reheat gently in a skillet to restore texture.
